scope.description: One probe on a three-voter cluster in which node 1 is a bare raft leader, node 2 a bare raft follower and node 3 is driven through the Node API. After the member control and the removal applied on node 3, the probe issues one proposal with a deadline context and one with context.Background from a goroutine, observes the background call for a fixed window, then stops the node and records how the blocked call ends.
assumptions: The harness plays the application loop for node 3 and the transport for all messages, delivering peer messages through Node.Step so that the Node-driven raft instance is only touched by its owning goroutine.
Node 1 is made leader directly by becomeCandidate/becomeLeader and then broadcasts its entry, which is the same leader state a completed election produces.
The non-expiring proposal is made from a separate goroutine so the test can observe whether it returns, and the observation window is 300 ms.
The derived field returned_within_window is the result of a select between the goroutine's result and a timer; the error text reported with it is the verbatim value the call would return.
Delivery is fault-free and in-process; no restart, snapshot or leadership change occurs, and stopping the node is the only intervention in the witness phase.
excluded: Caller contexts cancelled by a server shutdown other than the node stop exercised here
ReadOnlyLeaseBased, snapshots, restarts and joint configurations
The embedding service's own proposal timeouts, retries and membership tracking

basis.prefix: Harness (draft file assurance_generated_test.go, package raft, execution package '.'; no captured file is replaced). The test builds three storages for voters {1,2,3}: bare raft instances for nodes 1 and 2 and a RawNode wrapped in newNode for node 3, whose run loop the test starts and later stops explicitly. A delivery pump sends each message to the instance it addresses, feeding node 3's messages through Node.Step, and a drive loop hands node 3's Readys back with storage.Append and Node.Advance, applies committed conf-change entries through Node.ApplyConfChange and queues the Ready's messages. The probe makes node 1 leader and drives until both bare followers committed the leadership entry, emitting node_setup for probe_id 'member' with leader, term, committed, node3_in_config and the 200 ms call timeout; it then calls Node.Propose on node 3 with a 200 ms context and emits node_propose with the error text, elapsed milliseconds, the timeout, the derived blocked_until_deadline and node3_in_config. It proposes a ConfChangeV2 removing node 3 on the bare leader, drives until node 3's configuration no longer contains it, and emits self_removal_applied with probe_id 'removed'. It repeats the deadline-context proposal and then starts a goroutine calling Node.Propose with context.Background, waits up to 300 ms for that call, and emits node_propose_witness with observation_ms, returned_within_window, the error text and node3_in_config; finally it stops the node, waits up to two seconds for the blocked call to end and emits node_propose_after_stop with returned_after_stop and the error text. The test asserts that the member control returns without error, that the deadline-context call blocks until the deadline, and that the background-context call does not return inside the window but does return once the node is stopped, so a change in any of these behaviours fails the harness instead of reshaping the evidence.
basis.responsibility: The Node API owns telling a caller whether a proposal can be admitted. When the library itself has learned that the node is no longer a member, a proposal call that cannot be processed must be reported as not admissible rather than remaining blocked until the node is stopped, leaving the caller to infer the reason from its own termination logic.

comparisons.description: A proposal issued with a non-expiring caller context on a node that applied its own removal returns inside the fixed observation window.
Control: while the node is still a member, the deadline-context proposal returns promptly without error.

before.description: One probe on a three-voter cluster in which node 1 is a bare raft leader, node 2 a bare raft follower and node 3 is driven through the Node API. The probe first proposes through node 3's Node while it is still a member, then removes node 3 on the leader, lets node 3's application apply the committed entry, and repeats the same proposal with the same caller timeout.
assumptions: The harness plays the application loop for node 3 (handing Ready structs back with Advance) and the transport for all messages, delivering peer messages to node 3 through Node.Step so that raft state is only touched by the owning goroutine for the Node-driven node.
Node 1 is made leader directly by becomeCandidate/becomeLeader and then broadcasts its entry, which is the same leader state a completed election produces.
The subject's proposal is made through Node.Propose, the same call an embedding service uses, with a context that expires after the recorded timeout.
The derived field blocked_until_deadline is computed as (returned error == context.DeadlineExceeded) and (elapsed >= timeout/2); both operands are reported.
Delivery is fault-free and in-process; no restart, snapshot or leadership change occurs.
excluded: A non-expiring caller context, which the harness does not measure directly
